recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-30792 unless BRR later revisits the target profile or cardinality for RegulatedAuthorization.indication.
issue_request: FHIR-30792 was a Published/Persuasive BRR R5 request to change RegulatedAuthorization.indication, filed under the older MedicinalProductAuthorization artifact name, from a CodeableConcept/reference choice to a CodeableReference.
initial_application: Before the BRR decision, commit 33b409a4b6 had RegulatedAuthorization.indication[x] with CodeableConcept and Reference(ClinicalUseIssue). Commit 9765a2c28472d45bc31a92cce4687d7c87f338ca on 2021-02-14 changed the element to RegulatedAuthorization.indication with type CodeableReference, apparently applying the issue without naming the Jira key.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps RegulatedAuthorization active and redirects MedicinalProductAuthorization to RegulatedAuthorization. Later source refactoring retained CodeableReference while changing the target profile to ClinicalUseDefinition and the cardinality to 0..*. Searches found old choice element names only in historical release snapshots under tools/history, not in active current source. BRR Confluence minutes corroborate the Jira acceptance, and no conflicting Zulip or Confluence rationale was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the authoritative current StructureDefinition already has RegulatedAuthorization.indication typed as CodeableReference with a ClinicalUseDefinition target profile.
